name: GnollHack Player Assistance Benchmark Suite
description:
Eighteen questions across six Simple, six Intermediate, and six Advanced difficulty tiers, evaluating domain knowledge an Overseer assistant needs to assist players effectively.

### Covered Domains
- **Character & World**: Character creation, playable Gnoll race, difficulty levels, and saving throws.
- **Equipment & Items**: Weapon/armor quality modifiers (Exceptional, Elite, alignment tiers), object materials, dragon scale mail, and identify scrolls.
- **Magic & Mechanics**: Mana-based 12-school spell system, runewords, prayer timeouts, and sacrifice gifts.
- **Bestiary & Core**: Red dragon and Master Kaen profiles, multi-layer glyph rendering model, and dynamic monster scaling.

### Design & Rubrics
Questions are designed to be answerable without live game state and deliberately target mechanics where GnollHack **diverges from NetHack** (the primary failure mode for general LLMs). Each question rubric is anchored directly to the GnollHack C core source or official wiki, providing strict BARS criteria for accuracy, completeness, conciseness, and readability with defined critical error penalties.

questions.questionText: I want to roll a Gnoll character in GnollHack. What is the Gnoll race, which roles can play it, and what racial traits does it give me?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - The Gnoll is a GnollHack-original playable race that REPLACES the gnome of NetHack; GnollHack has no playable gnomes. Gnoll racial attribute maxima are Str 18/100, Int 16, Wis 16, Dex 19, Con 19, Cha 16, with minima of 3 in every attribute. Gnolls may be neutral or chaotic, never lawful. Racial traits: keen smell and a taste for tripe; they smell rotten food; they smell underground roots; they recognize corpse properties; they get TRIPLE nutrition from a tripe ration; and they can eat bones. Gnoll monster forms exist for mummy and zombie variants.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - presenting gnomes as playable in GnollHack; giving a lawful Gnoll; inventing racial intrinsics such as infravision-only or poison resistance that are not in the list above
SCOPE (conciseness) - role-by-role starting inventory is not required here; naming which roles admit Gnolls (Barbarian does, via MH_GNOLL) is enough without enumerating every role's restrictions
FORM (readability) - a short attribute table plus a bulleted trait list
SOURCE - src/role.c, gnoll race entry around line 1217; GnollHack wiki, 'How GnollHack differs from NetHack' (Gnoll replaces Gnome)

questions.questionText: In GnollHack, what do the Exceptional, Elite, Celestial, Primordial and Infernal weapon quality modifiers do to a weapon's damage, and are there any restrictions on using them?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - Quality modifiers MULTIPLY the weapon's base damage dice. Exceptional deals 2x base damage, Elite 3x, and Celestial, Primordial and Infernal each deal 4x. The 4x tiers are alignment-restricted: Celestial can be used only by lawful beings, Primordial only by neutral, Infernal only by chaotic. The multiplier applies to the dice, so a long sword that normally deals 1d8 against small and 1d12 against large deals 2d8 and 2d12 when exceptional. These modifiers can appear on melee weapons, ranged weapons and launchers, thrown weapons, ammunition, polearms, spiked shields, spiked gauntlets, magical gauntlets, spiked boots and kicking boots.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - describing the modifiers as flat damage bonuses or as enchantment (+1, +2) rather than dice multipliers; omitting the alignment restriction on the three 4x tiers; claiming this is a NetHack mechanic
SCOPE (conciseness) - armor quality modifiers, mythic and legendary items and elemental enchantments are separate systems and are out of scope beyond a one-line mention
FORM (readability) - a table of tier to multiplier to restriction
SOURCE - GnollHack wiki, 'Exceptional, Elite, Celestial, Primordial, and Infernal Items'

questions.questionText: What are the stats and properties of silver dragon scale mail in GnollHack?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - Weight 550 and a delay of 5 are fixed by the dragon-armor macro, not per item. Base AC 1, magic cancellation 4, cost 6000, spellcasting penalty 5, material dragon hide, body-armor slot, magical. It confers TWO properties: cold resistance AND reflection.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - quoting NetHack's weight of 40 or base AC of 9; naming reflection as the only conferred property and omitting cold resistance
SCOPE (conciseness) - the other dragon scale mails deserve at most a one-line contrast. If the answer notes that red dragon scale mail grants fire IMMUNITY rather than resistance, that is real knowledge of GnollHack's immunity-versus-resistance distinction and should count in its favour, not as padding
FORM (readability) - a short property table
SOURCE - src/objects.c, DRGN_ARMR macro lines 1198-1200 and the silver entry lines 1207-1210

questions.questionText: Which runewords exist in GnollHack, what does each one do, and where does each one work?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - There are exactly THREE runewords. Elbereth frightens hostile monsters and stops them attacking, and works OUTSIDE Gehennom. Gilthoniel protects items on the floor from being picked up by monsters, OUTSIDE Gehennom. Morgoth does the same item protection INSIDE Gehennom. They are engraved with the Engrave command, using fingers (dust, or blood for demons and vampires) or an inventory item; GnollHack also offers a Quick Engrave shortcut for preset words. Gilthoniel and Morgoth engravings do not smudge when walked over.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - naming Elbereth as the only runeword in GnollHack; swapping the Gehennom/non-Gehennom domains of Gilthoniel and Morgoth; claiming Gilthoniel or Morgoth frighten monsters (they protect items)
SCOPE (conciseness) - the full durability comparison of engraving tools belongs to a different question; one sentence is enough here
FORM (readability) - a three-row table of runeword, effect and where it works
SOURCE - GnollHack wiki, 'Runewords'; include/hack.h lines 826-827; src/monmove.c onnopickup

questions.questionText: How does prayer timeout work in GnollHack, and how long do I actually have to wait before it is safe to pray again?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - Prayer timeout is a hidden counter that decreases by 1 each turn. It starts at 150 for Priests and 300 for every other role. After a successful prayer it is reset from a base of 175 for Priests and 350 for other roles, randomised around that base. How far it must fall before praying is safe depends on your trouble: with a MAJOR trouble it is safe at timeout <= 200, with a MINOR trouble at <= 100, and with NO trouble only at <= 0. Killing the Wizard of Yendor or being crowned adds a large penalty per violation, roughly +500 for Priests and +1000 for other roles.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - quoting NetHack's ~800-1000 turn figures; giving a single safe threshold regardless of trouble; claiming the counter increases over time
SCOPE (conciseness) - the full catalogue of troubles and their remedies is not required; naming the three trouble tiers is enough
FORM (readability) - tables for the role values and for the trouble thresholds
SOURCE - GnollHack wiki, 'Praying'

questions.questionText: In GnollHack, how many items does a scroll of identify identify, and does its blessed, uncursed or cursed state change that?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - The count is fixed by BUC state, not by chance: cursed identifies 1 item, uncursed 2, and blessed 3. The implementation is cval = sblessed ? 3 : scursed ? 1 : 2, passed to identify_pack(). There is no whole-pack identify and no random proportion. Confused reading takes a separate branch. The scroll of identify is in the 'nodisappear' set, so it is not consumed the way most scrolls are.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - claiming a blessed scroll identifies the whole inventory or a random 20-100% (that is NetHack); claiming an uncursed scroll identifies exactly one item
SCOPE (conciseness) - other scrolls, price identification and general BUC mechanics are out of scope
FORM (readability) - a three-row table of BUC state to item count; this is the clearest possible shape for this answer and should score well on readability
SOURCE - src/read.c lines 2786-2789, and line 462 for nodisappear

questions.questionText: I am casting a fear spell at a monster in GnollHack. What determines whether the monster resists it, and how does this differ from NetHack?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - This is one of GnollHack's clearest departures from NetHack. Charm, sleep, fear and other mind-affecting spells and effects do NOT check the target's magic resistance. Instead the target makes a WISDOM-BASED SAVING THROW. The base chance to resist is -30% + 5% x Wisdom, giving 0% at Wis 6, 20% at Wis 10, 40% at Wis 14, 60% at Wis 18, 75% at Wis 21 and 95% at Wis 25. The caster's proficiency in the relevant spell school then modifies that chance: Unskilled +15%, Basic 0%, Skilled -15%, Expert -30%, Master -45%, Grand Master -60%. So a Grand Master caster reduces a Wis 18 monster's 60% resistance to effectively 0%. Wand skill applies an analogous modifier when the effect comes from a wand.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - saying that magic resistance governs these effects (that is NetHack, and it is the single most important thing to get right here); inverting the sign of the skill modifiers so that higher skill helps the target; inventing a Charisma- or Intelligence-based save
SCOPE (conciseness) - the full spell list and damage formulas are out of scope; a worked example is welcome but one is enough
FORM (readability) - the formula stated explicitly, plus a small table of Wisdom values and one of skill modifiers
SOURCE - GnollHack wiki, 'Saving Throws'

questions.questionText: A new player asks which GnollHack difficulty level to choose. What are the difficulty levels, how do they change the game mechanically, and what would you recommend?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - GnollHack has SEVEN difficulty levels: Standard, Experienced, Adept, Veteran, Expert, Master and Grand Master. Expert is the 100% baseline. Each level sets a combat difficulty percentage, scales the damage monsters deal and the damage you deal, and applies a score multiplier: Standard 9.9% combat difficulty, monsters deal 35% of normal, you deal 350%, score multiplier 1.0%; Experienced 17% / 45% / 255% / 3.3%; Adept 31% / 59% / 187% / 10%; Veteran 56% / 76% / 136% / 33%; Expert 100% / 100% / 100% / 100%; Master 177% / 130% / 73% / 200%; Grand Master 316% / 169% / 53% / 400%. Difficulty also affects starting resources. Difficulty level is separate from GAMEPLAY MODE (Casual, Classic, Casual-Classic, Modern, Tournament), and a good answer keeps the two apart. A sensible recommendation for a newcomer is a low difficulty such as Standard or Experienced, noting the low score multiplier as the trade-off.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - claiming NetHack-style single difficulty; inventing difficulty names; conflating difficulty levels with gameplay modes as if they were one setting; reversing the direction of the damage scaling
SCOPE (conciseness) - the full starting-inventory table per difficulty is not required; the mechanical axes and a recommendation are
FORM (readability) - a table of the seven levels against the four modifiers, then one or two sentences of advice
SOURCE - GnollHack wiki, 'Difficulty Levels' and 'Choosing the Right Difficulty Level'

questions.questionText: Explain GnollHack's spell system: what spell schools exist, what determines casting success, and how is this different from NetHack's spellcasting?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - GnollHack replaces NetHack's spell-retention model with a resource-based system: mana, material components (reagents) prepared with the Mix command, casting times and cooldowns, and over 200 spells. Spells are learned from spellbooks or by paying Priest and Artificer NPCs. There are 14 spell LEVELS: minor cantrip ('c', level -1), major cantrip ('C', level 0), and levels 1 through 12. There are TWELVE spell schools, each tied to one or more mental attributes and each either somatic or non-somatic: Abjuration (Int/Wis, non-somatic), Arcane (Int, somatic), Celestial (Wis/Cha, non-somatic), Clerical (Wis/Cha, non-somatic), Conjuration (Int/Cha, somatic), Divination (any, non-somatic), Enchantment (Int/Cha, non-somatic), Healing (Wis, non-somatic), Movement (Int/Wis, somatic), Nature (Wis/Cha, non-somatic), Necromancy (Wis/Cha, non-somatic), Transmutation (any, somatic). Where a school lists several attributes the HIGHEST is used for the success bonus. Armor imposes a somatic penalty on casting.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - saying spells are forgotten over time (GnollHack removed that); giving NetHack's seven spell categories; inventing school names not in the list of twelve; claiming casting is a single chance roll with no mana
SCOPE (conciseness) - individual spell descriptions are out of scope; naming the schools and the system's shape is what is wanted
FORM (readability) - a table of the twelve schools with their attributes and somatic flag
SOURCE - GnollHack wiki, 'Spell Casting' and 'How GnollHack differs from NetHack'

questions.questionText: I found a suit of body armor made of an unusual material in GnollHack. What do the special object materials do, and which ones should I be looking for?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - GnollHack can generate weapons, tools and armor in a material other than their normal one, and the material changes the item's properties. For armor: dragonhide gives -2 AC and +1 MC on body armor and -1 AC and +1 MC elsewhere; steel gives -1 AC on all armor; silver has no direct effect but matters against demons and similar; hard crystal grants REFLECTION on body armor, adds 4/3 enchantability, applies a 0.2x spellcasting-penalty multiplier and a further 30% penalty reduction on body armor; gemstone gives -4 AC on body armor and -3 elsewhere plus 4/3 enchantability; bronze gives +1 AC and +3 MC on body armor only, plus 4/3 enchantability; orichalcum gives +7 MC on body armor and +2 elsewhere, grants MAGIC RESISTANCE on body armor, weighs 75% of normal and has half enchantability; mithril gives -3 AC and +2 MC on body armor and -2 AC and +1 MC elsewhere. Note that lower AC is better and that bronze's +1 AC is therefore a penalty traded against a large MC gain.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - presenting materials as cosmetic; asserting that mithril or another material grants magic resistance when orichalcum is the one that does; getting the sign of AC backwards while drawing conclusions from it
SCOPE (conciseness) - weapon material effects and the full material list can be summarised; the armor materials above are the required content
FORM (readability) - a material table with AC, MC and special-property columns
SOURCE - GnollHack wiki, 'Object Materials'

questions.questionText: How does ranged and melee combat in GnollHack differ from NetHack in ways that change how I should actually fight?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - Several concrete divergences, all of which change tactics. Weapon swapping is INSTANT rather than costing a turn, so switching between melee and ranged sets mid-fight is free. Launchers ADD their own damage to the missile, so the bow or crossbow matters, not just the ammunition - the opposite of NetHack. The skill cap is raised to GRAND MASTER, and weapon skill increases CRITICAL HIT CHANCE rather than only to-hit and damage. GnollHack adds dual-wielded artifacts, spiked shields and main-gauches. Encounters are scaled rather than allowing NetHack's early out-of-depth swarms, and many insta-deaths are DELAYED, giving the player turns in which to react. Quality modifiers (exceptional, elite and the alignment-restricted tiers) multiply weapon damage dice.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - claiming weapon swapping costs a turn or that launchers contribute no damage (both are the NetHack rules); giving NetHack's Expert skill cap as GnollHack's maximum; asserting invented to-hit formulas as source fact
SCOPE (conciseness) - a complete weapons table is not wanted. Four or five precise, correct divergences beat an exhaustive survey, and an answer that pads with generic roguelike advice should lose conciseness points
FORM (readability) - a NetHack-versus-GnollHack comparison table
SOURCE - GnollHack wiki, 'How GnollHack differs from NetHack'; 'Exceptional, Elite, Celestial, Primordial, and Infernal Items'

questions.questionText: In GnollHack, which pieces of armor can carry a quality modifier, and what do Exceptional and Elite give to body armor as opposed to shields?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - Quality modifiers on armor improve BOTH AC and MC. They can appear on body armor (non-magical and semi-magical body armor only), on all shields including the shield of reflection, on all boots including magical boots, and on all gloves including magical gloves. For BODY ARMOR: Exceptional gives -4 AC and +1 MC, Elite -8 AC and +2 MC, and Celestial/Primordial/Infernal -12 AC and +4 MC restricted to lawful/neutral/chaotic wearers respectively. For SHIELDS: Exceptional -3 AC and +1 MC, Elite -6 AC and +2 MC, Celestial/Primordial/Infernal -9 AC and +3 MC with the same alignment restrictions. Lower AC is better, so these are improvements.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - claiming fully magical body armor can carry a quality modifier; giving the shield numbers for body armor or vice versa; treating the AC change as a penalty
SCOPE (conciseness) - the weapon multipliers are a different question; one line of contrast is enough
FORM (readability) - two small tables, one for body armor and one for shields
SOURCE - GnollHack wiki, 'Exceptional, Elite, Celestial, Primordial, and Infernal Items'

questions.questionText: Give me the complete combat profile of the red dragon in GnollHack, including everything that would change how I fight or use one.
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - The monster is named 'red dragon'; GnollHack has no separate 'adult red dragon', and an answer that says so is more accurate than one that adopts a NetHack naming convention. Stats: level 17, speed 9, AC -1, magic cancellation 10, magic resistance 20, alignment -4, base difficulty 20. Attacks: 6d6 fire breath, 3d8 bite, and two 1d4 claws. Size gigantic, 1500 nutrition, roar sound, one head, flesh. Resistances: fire, see invisible and REGENERATION, plus slime resistance, with fire magic cancellation. Behavioural flags: flies, thick hide, oviparous, carnivore, and critically M1_STEED - a red dragon CAN BE RIDDEN in GnollHack. Also bonevore, speaking, greedy for gold and gems, magic-using and brave.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - quoting NetHack's figures (level 15, 4d6 breath); omitting fire resistance; stating it cannot be used as a steed; omitting regeneration, which materially changes a long fight
SCOPE (conciseness) - dragon scale mail and the other dragon colours are out of scope
FORM (readability) - a stat table plus an attack list
SOURCE - src/monst.c lines 2664-2677; LVL/SIZ/STATS macros at src/monst.c lines 73-75

questions.questionText: I am preparing to face Master Kaen in GnollHack. What exactly am I up against?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - Defined with the MON macro in src/monst.c around line 6519, symbol class S_HUMAN, title 'monk'. LVL(25, 16, -10, 15, 10, -20): level 25, speed 16, AC -10, magic cancellation 15, and MAGIC RESISTANCE OF ONLY 10 - low for his level, which is the tactically important and counter-intuitive fact. Generation flags G_NOGEN | G_UNIQ, so he is never randomly generated. Attacks in order: AT_CLAW/AD_PHYS 16d2, a second identical 16d2 claw, AT_MAGC/AD_CLRC clerical spellcasting, and AT_CLAW/AD_SAMU 1d4 which steals the Amulet. Human weight, 400 nutrition, nemesis sound, human size, one head. STATS(STR18(100), 19, 19, 19, 19, 19) in (str, dex, con, int, wis, cha) order. Resistances: poison, stoning, see invisible, charm and stun, with poison magic cancellation. Flags include humanoid, herbivore, no-polymorph, human, male, hostile, nasty, stalking, item-collecting, magic-using, wants-artifact, waits-for-you, infravisible, speaking, proper name, boss monster and monk. Difficulty 40.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - claiming high magic resistance (it is 10); reciting NetHack's attack tuples; omitting the amulet-stealing AD_SAMU attack; claiming he can be randomly generated
SCOPE (conciseness) - the Monk quest storyline is out of scope; tactical advice is welcome only if it follows from the stats given
FORM (readability) - a stat table plus an attack table
SOURCE - src/monst.c lines 6519-6530

questions.questionText: Explain GnollHack's multi-layer glyph rendering model: what layers exist, where they are defined, and how the C core hands them to the client.
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - The enum is 'layer_types' and it is defined in include/layer.h, NOT in display.h. There are twenty layers before MAX_LAYERS, in order: LAYER_FLOOR, LAYER_CARPET, LAYER_FLOOR_DOODAD, LAYER_FEATURE, LAYER_TRAP, LAYER_FEATURE_DOODAD, LAYER_BACKGROUND_EFFECT, LAYER_CHAIN, LAYER_OBJECT, LAYER_MONSTER, LAYER_MISSILE, LAYER_COVER_TRAP, LAYER_COVER_OBJECT, LAYER_COVER_FEATURE, LAYER_LEASH, LAYER_ENVIRONMENT, LAYER_ZAP, LAYER_GENERAL_EFFECT, LAYER_MONSTER_EFFECT, LAYER_GENERAL_UI. struct layer_info carries layer_glyphs[MAX_LAYERS] and layer_gui_glyphs[MAX_LAYERS] side by side - an ASCII-compatible set and a GUI set - plus layer_flags, m_id and o_id used to check that the monster or boulder being drawn is the one actually there, and memory_objchn for remembered objects. The core publishes glyphs through show_glyph_on_layer() and show_gui_glyph_on_layer(), declared in include/extern.h.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - stating there are only four or five layers; placing the enum in display.h; inventing layer names that are not in the list above
SCOPE (conciseness) - the SkiaSharp drawing code lives in the separate .NET MAUI client repository and is NOT in this source tree. A brief, clearly-labelled statement about the client side is appropriate; extended invented detail about it is not and should be marked down
FORM (readability) - an ordered list of the layers, bottom to top, then a short paragraph on struct layer_info
SOURCE - include/layer.h lines 13-36; include/extern.h lines 577-581

questions.questionText: In the GnollHack C source, how are monster level and group size scaled to the player and the dungeon depth when monsters are generated?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - The scaling logic is in src/makemon.c; src/monst.c is the monster DATA table and contains no such logic. adj_lev(), commented 'adjust strength of monsters based on u.uz and u.ulevel' around line 3976, computes the adjusted level, and makemon applies it around line 2573 as m_lev = adj_lev(ptr, level_adjustment). The eligible monster-level band is computed in FLOATING POINT from the dungeon level and u.ulevel together, with per-branch caps and multipliers - the minimum is capped at 25 or 15 depending on branch, and the maximum is scaled by factors such as 1.189 and 1.414 - around lines 3716-3727. Group sizes are reduced for low-level heroes: cntdiv = (u.ulevel < 3) ? 4 : (u.ulevel < 5) ? 2 : 1, around lines 112-119. Eligibility is further governed by the G_NOGEN, G_UNIQ and G_GENO flags and the per-monster generation frequency in the data table.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - attributing the computation to monst.c; presenting NetHack's integer-only formula as GnollHack's; claiming difficulty is a single stored field rather than computed; inventing function names
SCOPE (conciseness) - mkclass, special-level generation and specific monster placement are out of scope
FORM (readability) - prose naming the identifiers, with the two formulas quoted verbatim
SOURCE - src/makemon.c lines 112-119, 2573, 3716-3727 and 3976-3978

questions.questionText: How do sacrifice gifts work in GnollHack? What do I need before my god will give me one, and how does the chance change as the game goes on?
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - A sacrifice gift is a reward for offering a fresh, acceptable corpse at an altar; gifts are typically artifacts, or high-quality utility or power items as replacement rewards. Three conditions must hold: character level 3 or higher; luck 0 or higher (non-negative); and sacrificing at an altar of your own alignment, with gifts normally given only while in good standing. When those hold, the chance of a gift is 1 / (10 + 2 x Gifts x Artifacts), where Gifts is the number of gifts already received and Artifacts is the TOTAL number of artifacts generated in the game - not only the ones you were given. So the first gift is a 1-in-10 chance and subsequent gifts become rapidly less likely, because both factors grow.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - stating a flat or constant gift chance; using only the player's own artifacts in place of the total generated; dropping the luck or level requirement; quoting NetHack's sacrifice-gift rules as GnollHack's
SCOPE (conciseness) - the corpse freshness rules, cross-aligned conversion and same-race sacrifice penalties can be mentioned briefly but are not the required content
FORM (readability) - the formula stated explicitly, plus a short bullet list of the three conditions; a worked example of the first two gifts reads well
SOURCE - GnollHack wiki, 'Sacrifice Gifts'

questions.questionText: Under exactly what conditions does an engraved Elbereth fail to protect me in GnollHack? Answer at the level of the implementation.
questions.expectedPoints:
REQUIRED (accuracy + completeness) - Elbereth protects ONLY the square the hero is standing on, or the square the hero's displaced image occupies; an engraving on any other square does nothing for the player. It is ignored by shopkeepers, by vault guards, by blinded monsters, by peaceful monsters, by EVERY monster of the S_HUMAN symbol class, and by any monster whose data satisfies ignores_Elbereth(). It has no effect at all in Gehennom or anywhere in the endgame. The check also gates the fleeing behaviour on attack, so a monster already adjacent is not exempt by proximity. Engraving durability follows the engraving TYPE: DUST 1 (a finger, fragile and smudged by walking), ENGRAVE 2 (an athame or similar edged tool), BURN 3 (a wand of fire or lightning, the most durable), MARK 4 (a magic marker); GnollHack additionally has ENGR_FLAGS_NON_SMUDGING, which is what keeps Gilthoniel and Morgoth engravings intact.
CRITICAL ERROR (set criticalError) - claiming Elbereth protects any square regardless of where the hero stands; claiming it works in Gehennom or the endgame; omitting that all human-class monsters ignore it; describing NetHack's erosion-on-attack behaviour as GnollHack's
SCOPE (conciseness) - the runeword list itself is a different question; Gilthoniel and Morgoth need only a passing mention here
FORM (readability) - prose for the failure conditions, then a small table of engraving type to durability
SOURCE - src/monmove.c lines 445-475; include/engrave.h lines 19-28; src/mon.c line 4819
